sources.headings: BS Computer Science, Test Requirements, LCAT Guidelines
sources.doc:
The LCAT is a paper-based, multiple-choice test, similar to the SAT, though it may differ in terms of duration and format.
  * **Number of Sections:** 4 (two verbal and two math sections)
  * **Duration:** The duration of each section is 40 minutes, with a total test duration of approximately 3 hours.
  * **Test Mode:** LCAT is a paper-based test.
  * **Calculators:** Not allowed during any part of the test.


**Verbal Sections**
The Verbal Sections of the LCAT evaluate critical reading and writing skills essential for academic and professional success. These sections test comprehension, analysis, and effective communication through various content domains, including Craft and Structure, Information and Ideas, Standard English Conventions, and Expression of Ideas. Applicants are encouraged to practice reading comprehension, text analysis, and editing for clarity and accuracy.
**Math Sections**
The Math Sections of the LCAT evaluate essential mathematical skills required for higher education, focusing on Algebra, Advanced Mathematics, Problem-Solving and Data Analysis, and Geometry and Trigonometry, which are critical for success in higher education. These sections test quantitative reasoning, data interpretation, and problem-solving abilities. Applicants are advised to strengthen foundational concepts, practice problem-solving without calculators, and review SAT-style materials for effective preparation.
[Click here](https://lums.edu.pk/sites/default/files/sample_lcat_2025.pdf) to access the LCAT guidelines and explore sample questions for both the Math and Verbal sections.

sources.headings: BS Computer Science, Important Note
sources.doc:
1. LUMS will only accept scores of the Admission Test(s) mentioned above for the Fall 2026 applications.
  2. **SAT/ACT** taken after the stipulated deadlines will not be considered for the Fall 2026 admissions.
  3. **SAT** taken before **March 2024** will not be considered for Fall 2026 admissions.
  4. **ACT** taken before **February 2024** will not be considered for Fall 2026 admissions.
  5. While registering for the SAT/ACT/LCAT, use your name as it appears on your LUMS Online application and other academic credentials. Using a different name may prevent your scores from matching the rest of your application in our database.
  6. **Official SAT scores** of all applicants must be submitted by the testing agency, i.e.,**ETS** , directly to the LUMS Admissions Office. Applicants must request ETS to send a direct report to LUMS. The college code for reporting SAT scores to LUMS is **0513**.
  7. **Official ACT scores** must be submitted directly to the LUMS Admissions Office by the testing agency, i.e., American College Testing Service (ACT), USA. The college code for reporting ACT scores to LUMS is **7896**.
  8. Applicants are required to report test scores of all attempts through an online application and must submit a copy of the score report(s) to the University. Scores and attempts not reported through the LUMS Online application will not be considered valid for evaluation.
  9. **The best score of a single attempt** (SAT and/or ACT) will be considered for application evaluation.
  10. Applicants are required to submit score(s) of the SAT and/or ACT to the LUMS Admissions Office soon after the announcement of the results. A copy of a “**Student Report** ” should also be uploaded online.
  11. LCAT Scores will be valid only for **One (1) academic year**.
  12. LCAT scores will be used for application evaluation and, hence, will not be disclosed to applicants.
  13. Applicants taking the LUMS Admission Test(s), and those who have also taken (or are planning to take) the SAT and/or ACT tests are encouraged to submit a copy of their standardized test score report(s) as part of their admission application. A copy of the scores should be uploaded online along with all other supporting documents, or reported directly from the Testing Agency.

item.query: فاسٹ میں میرٹ اسکالرشپ کس کو ملتی ہے اور کیا کور کرتی ہے؟
item.gt: Top three position holders of each examination board and top three on the NU admission merit list of each campus; equal to full tuition fee for four years; requires semester GPA of 3.0 or above

result.answer:
FAST National University میں میرٹ اسکالرشپ صرف ٹاپ تھری پوزیشن ہولڈرز کو ملی جاتی ہے۔ اس میں بطور ایک حکمت عملی کے ہر ایک ایکساس نیشن بورڈ کے ٹاپ تھری پوزیشن ہولڈرز کو دیا جاتا ہے۔ FAST National University ان اڈمنیٹشن مرٹ لسٹ میں ٹاپ تھری پوزیشن ہولڈرز کو بھی اسکالرشپ دیتی ہے۔

اس اسکالرشپ کا مقصد یونیورسٹی کے ٹوٹل کرسٹس کیا گیا ہے، جو پوری ٹوٹیشن فیس کو ڈک کرتا ہے۔ یہ اسکالرشپ چار سال کے لیے ہے۔

میرٹ اسکالرشپ کے لیے سلیکشن کے بعد جی پی اے ≥3.0 رہا ضروری ہے۔ اگر کسی کو کورس میں فیل ہو یا وائڈrawn ہو، تو اسکالرشپ معاف ہو جاتی ہے اور یہ کورسز میں کرسٹ نہیں ہوتے۔

claims.text: Merit scholarship is awarded to the Top Three position holders of each Examination Board in the year of admission.
Merit Scholarship is also offered to Top Three position holders in the merit list of NU admission merit list of each campuses.
The scholarship is equal to the full tuition fee.
The scholarship is for four years of uninterrupted studies.

sources.headings: 1. Merit Scholarships for Bachelor Students
sources.doc:
Merit scholarship is awarded to the Top Three position holders of each Examination Board in the year of admission.
Merit Scholarship is also offered to Top Three position holders in the merit list of NU admission merit list of each campuses.
The University awards certificates and cash prizes to those undergraduate students, who are the Top Three in their department. Students are selected from each of the four years of every degree program.   
  
This scholarship is for four years of un-interrupted studies with standard courses (core and elective), labs and final year projects of the degree offered by the department in a semester to a batch with a specified number of total credit hours and is equal to the full tuition fee. 
A student registering for less or more credit hours than the total specified number of credit hours shall not be eligible for Merit Scholarship. Student must not have failed, repeated or withdrawn from a course in that semester.   
  
If there are more than one student in the same position, the next position will automatically be vanished or moved down depending on the number of students in one position.   
  
**Continuation of merit scholarship is subject to maintaining semester GPA of 3.0 or higher.**

sources.headings: 5. HEC Scholarships for MS and PhD students
sources.doc: The Higher Education Commission (HEC) provides liberal scholarships to students desirous of studying for MS and PhD degrees at this university. The scholarship covers tuition fee, monthly stipend, and book allowance.

sources.headings: 4. Punjab Honhaar Scholarship Program
sources.doc: The Honhaar Scholarship Program, an initiative of the Punjab Higher Education Commission, aims to provide financial assistance to deserving and meritorious students pursuing higher education at universities and colleges in Punjab, Pakistan. The program seeks to ensure equal access to quality education, particularly for those with limited financial resources.

sources.headings: 6. OSAF Scholarships
sources.doc: OSAF (Old Students Association of FAST) arranges financial assistance for those students who cannot afford to pay their full fee.

sources.headings: 3. Punjab Educational Endowment Fund (PEEF) Scholarships
sources.doc: The PEEF provides financial assistance to talented and needy students in Punjab and other provinces of Pakistan, including Azad Jammu & Kashmir, FATA, Gilgit Baltistan, and Islamabad Capital Territory. It aims to support students pursuing Intermediate, Graduation, and Master's level degrees. PEEF was established to address the gap in educational opportunities for deserving students by providing scholarships and other financial assistance.

sources.headings: 2. ICT Scholarships and Balochistan Endowment Scholarships
sources.doc: ICT Scholarships refer to the Prime Minister's National ICT Scholarship Program, a program by Ignite (formerly National ICT R&D Fund) that provides financial assistance to students pursuing ICT degrees. Balochistan Endowment Scholarships, specifically the Balochistan Education Endowment Fund (BEEF), aims to support the education of talented students from Balochistan, including those from less privileged backgrounds.

item.query: How does repayment of the FAST study loan work?
item.gt: Interest-free; repayment starts three months after graduation or on getting employment, whichever is earlier; repaid within four years

result.answer: At FAST-NU, interest-free study loans are available for bright indigent students. Repayment of the loan starts three months after graduation or soon after getting employment, whichever is earlier. The total amount has to be repaid within a period of four years after graduation. Students are required to sign a contract allowing future employers to deduct loan repayments at source and remit it to the University.

sources.headings: SAT Fee Waivers, Getting a Fee Waiver
sources.doc:
If you think you're eligible, talk to your school counselor about getting a fee waiver code or request a fee waiver directly from College Board. You may redeem one fee waiver code or receive benefits directly through College Board once per lifetime.
If you choose to request a fee waiver directly from College Board, please:
  * [Review the eligibility criteria.](https://satsuite.collegeboard.org/sat/registration/fee-waivers/fee-waiver-eligibility)
  * Read the [Fee Waiver: Student Self-Identification](https://satsuite.collegeboard.org/media/pdf/sat-fee-waiver-self-id.pdf) resource for an overview of the process.
  * Be mindful of registration deadlines and request fee waivers early so you can apply those benefits in a timely manner. Please aim to submit your request as early as possible and at least 1–2 weeks before the registration deadline.
  * Be prepared to share the contact information of an adult who can verify your eligibility. Please notify that adult that they may receive a verification email and ask them to respond to requests for verification as quickly as possible so you can pursue your next steps.
  * Talk to your school counselor if you have questions about the process.


Do you meet the eligibility criteria? If so, you can [request a fee waiver directly from College Board](https://satfeewaiverform.collegeboard.org/).
**Important:** When you’re filling out the form, please double-check that your address is accurate and correctly formatted. You will see instructions on how to format data correctly on the form itself.
A complete, accurate, and correctly formatted address helps us review your fee waiver request more efficiently, and it helps you avoid issues with registration or submitting your scores to colleges and scholarships.
**If your address is incomplete, inaccurate, or incorrectly formatted, your fee waiver request will be delayed.** If you need to update your address, you can do so in Account Settings before filling out the form.
Making sure you meet the eligibility criteria helps ensure we can continue to offer this benefit efficiently for qualified students.
**Providing false information about your eligibility for a fee waiver may result in a ban on your College Board student account, and we may prevent you from taking future College Board assessments (including, without limitation, the SAT, Advanced Placement (AP), and CLEP exams). Additionally, we may cancel your SAT registration or scores if you have already taken one of these assessments.**

sources.headings: SAT ID Requirements, Country-Specific, Testing Outside Your Home Country
sources.doc:
If you travel to another country to test, you must use a valid passport as your ID. The only exception to this policy is a U.S. Department of War (DoW) Common Access Card (CAC), which may be used instead of a passport.

The only acceptable forms of identification are a valid passport (with your name, photograph, and signature), a valid Ghana Card, or a U.S. Department of War (DoW) Common Access Card (CAC).

For students testing at HKEAA centers, the only acceptable form of identification is a valid (unexpired) photo ID that is government issued. School IDs are not acceptable.

The only acceptable forms of identification are a valid passport (with your name, photograph, and signature) or a U.S. Department of War (DoW) Common Access Card (CAC).

sources.headings: SAT ID Requirements, General Requirements, If You're 21 or Older
sources.doc: If you’ll be 21 or older on test day, the only acceptable form of identification is an official government-issued photo ID, such as a driver’s license or passport, that meets all the previous requirements on this page. Student ID cards aren’t valid forms of identification for test takers who are 21 or older.

item.query: What is FAST's fee refund policy?
item.gt: Tuition: 100% up to 10th day of classes, 80% to 15th, 60% to 20th, 50% to 30th, none from 31st; admission fee non-refundable; security deposit refundable

result.answer:
At FAST University, the fee refund policy depends on the type of fee and timing of withdrawal. The Admission Fee is non-refundable. The Security Deposit is refundable at the time of completion of degree or closing of admission. The Tuition Fee is refunded in accordance with the guidelines of the Higher Education Commission (HEC). If a student is admitted and then eligibility cannot be met after result declaration, fee refund is calculated from the date of result announcement. 

For tuition fee refunds, FAST follows this timeline based on days of class commencement (all days counted including working days and holidays): Up to 10th day - 100% Fee Refund; Up to 15th day - 80% Fee Refund; Up to 20th day - 60% Fee Refund; Up to 30th day - 50% Fee Refund; 31st day onwards - No Refund. 

Additional fees are non-refundable. If a graduate of this University is admitted to a higher degree program, the admission fee is not payable again.

sources.headings: Fee Refund Policy
sources.doc:
1. Admission Fee is non-refundable.  
2. Security deposit is refundable at the time of completion of degree or closing of admission.  
3. Tuition Fee is refunded in accordance with the guidelines of Higher Education Commission (HEC).   
| Timeline  | Percentage of Fee  |  
| --- | --- |  
| Upto 10th day of commencement of classes  | 100% Fee Refund  |  
| Upto 15th day of commencement of classes  | 80% Fee Refund  |  
| Upto 20th day of commencement of classes  | 60% Fee Refund  |  
| Upto 30th day of commencement of classes  | 50% Fee Refund  |  
| 31st day onwards of commencement of classes  | No Refund  |  
**Note:** Days shall be counted including working days and holidays.
After declaration of FSc/A Level/Equivalent result, admission of a student stands cancelled if he/she fails to meet the required eligibility requirement for admission. The fee refund is calculated from the date of his/her result announcement.

sources.headings: Frequently Asked Questions - FAST NUCES Admissions Fall 2026
sources.doc:
**Q:** How Can I Apply for Admission?
**A:** The procedure for admission is as follows: 
  * Apply online only through the official portal.
  * No applications via post or hand are accepted.
  * Each applicant receives a unique ARN (Application Reference Number).
  * Ensure all information is correct before submission.
  * **Verify all information carefully before making fee payment.**
  * Any changes after fee submission may incur processing charges.
  * Incorrect or false information may lead to cancellation without refund.
  * Admit card is generated after fee payment.
  * Candidate must appear at the scheduled test center.

**Important:** Admission of a student automatically stands cancelled if he or she fails in the required exam whose result was not available at the time of admission application. 
[🔗 https://nu.edu.pk/Degree-Programs](https://nu.edu.pk/Degree-Programs) [🔗 https://nu.edu.pk/Admissions/Schedule](https://nu.edu.pk/Admissions/Schedule)
**Q:** Which admission tests are accepted for Fall 2026?
**A:** Applicants may apply through: 
  * SAT/NTS **OR** NU Admission Test (Undergraduate Admissions)   
_(Applicant must select**only one** out of the three admission test options)_
  * HAT-1, 2 & 3 (Graduate Admissions) **OR** NU Admission Test   
_(Applicant must select**only one** out of the two admission test options)_
  * HAT-Subject for PhD **OR** NU Admission Test   
_(Applicant must select**only one** out of the two admission test options)_

**Q:** What is the fee per credit hour?
**A:** **Rs 12,000 per credit hour** (w.e.f Fall 2026, applicable to all batches) 
**Q:** How is semester fee calculated?
**A:** FAST does not have a fixed semester fee.  
Example: 
  * 15 credit hours × Rs. 12,000
  * Student Activity Fund

**Q:** Are there any additional fees?
**A:** At admission: 
  * Admission fee
  * Security deposit
  * First semester tuition fee
  * Student Activity Fund

Later semesters: 
  * Tuition fee
  * Student Activity Fund

**Q:** I cannot afford the fee. Is financial assistance available?
**A:** Yes: 
  * Need-based financial aid
  * Interest-free loans
  * Merit scholarships

**Q:** Can fees be paid in installments?
**A:** Yes, subject to approval by campus administration. 
**Q:** What is the refund policy?
**A:**
  * Admission fee is non-refundable
  * Security deposit is refundable at the time of completion of degree or closing of admission
  * Tuition Fee is refunded in accordance with the guidelines of HEC

[🔗 https://nu.edu.pk/Admissions/FeeStructure](https://nu.edu.pk/Admissions/FeeStructure)

**A:** Hostels are available at:

**A:** Yes, transport facility is available in all campuses.

**A:**

  * SMS/email notifications may also be sent

**Q:** I am a foreign student. How can I apply?
**A:**
  * Passport number can be used
  * Afghan students may use POR number

**Q:** Can I transfer from another university?
**A:** Yes: 
  * Apply as a normal applicant
  * Credit transfer after admission
  * Maximum 50% credits transferable (HEC rule)

**Q:** Can I migrate between campuses?
**A:** Yes, subject to: 
  * Merit
  * Seat availability
  * Approval

**Q:** Are classes held on weekends or evenings?
**A:**
  * Karachi offers weekend programs
  * Other campuses may offer limited evening/weekend classes

**Q:** How is merit calculated?
**A:**
  * Based on Admission Test / SAT / NTS / HAT **OR** NU Admission Test   
_(Applicant must select**only one** out of the three admission test options)_

[🔗 https://nu.edu.pk/Admissions/EligibilityCriteria](https://nu.edu.pk/Admissions/EligibilityCriteria)

**A:** Yes.

sources.headings: Admission Procedure
sources.doc:
The procedure for admission is as follows:
  1. Admission Application Form must be filled online by following the instructions.[ **Click Here** ](http://admissions.nu.edu.pk/) for Online Admission Application 
  2. Applications received through post or by hand will not be accepted/entertained.
  3. The online system assigns a unique Application Reference Number (ARN) to each applicant, which must be noted for later use.
  4. Applicant will confirm that information entered in the Admission Application Form is correct. **In case of incorrect information, the University has all the rights to cancel the application/admission without any fee refund.**
  5. Applicant will deposit the Application Fee in the designated Bank. **Fee is non-refundable/adjustable.**
  6. Upon payment of the Application Processing Fee (and additional Admission Test Fee), the applicant will print his/her **ADMIT CARD** bearing the applicant’s **TEST ROLL NUMBER**.
  7. The applicant should then visit the test campus on the specified date and time as mentioned on the Admit card.
  8. **Admission of a student automatically stands cancelled if he or she fails in the required exam whose result was not available at the time of admission.**

sources.headings: NU Online Admission Test for Graduate programs
sources.doc:
Information on various Admission Tests is available on the University’s admission web-site [ **admissions.nu.edu.pk** ](http://admissions.nu.edu.pk/)
The online admission test is taken on a computer. The candidate should be familiar with the use of mouse and the keyboard. Each candidate is given a different examination. The sections of a test (English, Analytical skills, Math etc) appear in a random sequence. Moreover, questions related to different topics also appear before the candidate in a random sequence. In each section, a candidate can move forward and backwards to review the responses selected. The candidate can change his or her response to any question within the current section.
Each section of the admission test has a fixed duration. Each section is timed independently and time saved in one section is not carried forward to the next sections. At the end of the test, a summary of the results is displayed on screen. The duration of the Online Admission Test is between two and three hours.
Applicants should reach the test centre on the date and time specified on the admit card. Latecomers will not be allowed to take the test. Applicants should not bring anything to the test centre except their Admit Cards. No applicant will be allowed to take the test without an endorsed Admit Card. The Admission Test is held at all campuses of the University (Karachi, Lahore, Islamabad, Peshawar, Chiniot-Faisalabad and Multan).

sources.headings: 1. Merit Scholarships for Bachelor Students
sources.doc:
Merit scholarship is awarded to the Top Three position holders of each Examination Board in the year of admission.
Merit Scholarship is also offered to Top Three position holders in the merit list of NU admission merit list of each campuses.
The University awards certificates and cash prizes to those undergraduate students, who are the Top Three in their department. Students are selected from each of the four years of every degree program.   
  
This scholarship is for four years of un-interrupted studies with standard courses (core and elective), labs and final year projects of the degree offered by the department in a semester to a batch with a specified number of total credit hours and is equal to the full tuition fee. 
A student registering for less or more credit hours than the total specified number of credit hours shall not be eligible for Merit Scholarship. Student must not have failed, repeated or withdrawn from a course in that semester.   
  
If there are more than one student in the same position, the next position will automatically be vanished or moved down depending on the number of students in one position.   
  
**Continuation of merit scholarship is subject to maintaining semester GPA of 3.0 or higher.**

sources.headings: 3. Rules for Internal Sponsorships:
sources.doc:
1. Internal sponsorships are available for studying in regular semesters (spring and Fall). Following is the maximum number of semesters for which it can be availed. 
     * Bachelors: 8 semesters
     * Masters: 4 semesters
     * PhD: 6 semesters
  2. It shall not be available for repeat or withdrawn courses. This implies that it is available for studying a course only once.
  3. It is suspended if the student’s CGPA falls below the minimum specified to avoid warning and shall be restored upon getting out of warning by improvement in CGPA.
  4. It shall be limited to tuition fee only.

**A:** The procedure for admission is as follows:

  * No applications via post or hand are accepted.

  * Ensure all information is correct before submission.
  * **Verify all information carefully before making fee payment.**
  * Any changes after fee submission may incur processing charges.
  * Incorrect or false information may lead to cancellation without refund.
  * Admit card is generated after fee payment.
  * Candidate must appear at the scheduled test center.

**Important:** Admission of a student automatically stands cancelled if he or she fails in the required exam whose result was not available at the time of admission application. 
[🔗 https://nu.edu.pk/Degree-Programs](https://nu.edu.pk/Degree-Programs) [🔗 https://nu.edu.pk/Admissions/Schedule](https://nu.edu.pk/Admissions/Schedule)
**Q:** Which admission tests are accepted for Fall 2026?
**A:** Applicants may apply through: 
  * SAT/NTS **OR** NU Admission Test (Undergraduate Admissions)   
_(Applicant must select**only one** out of the three admission test options)_
  * HAT-1, 2 & 3 (Graduate Admissions) **OR** NU Admission Test   
_(Applicant must select**only one** out of the two admission test options)_

_(Applicant must select**only one** out of the two admission test options)_

**A:** FAST does not have a fixed semester fee.  
Example: 
  * 15 credit hours × Rs. 12,000
  * Student Activity Fund

**A:** At admission: 
  * Admission fee
  * Security deposit
  * First semester tuition fee
  * Student Activity Fund

Later semesters:

**A:** Yes:

  * Interest-free loans

**A:**
  * Admission fee is non-refundable

sources.headings: 3. Punjab Educational Endowment Fund (PEEF) Scholarships
sources.doc: The PEEF provides financial assistance to talented and needy students in Punjab and other provinces of Pakistan, including Azad Jammu & Kashmir, FATA, Gilgit Baltistan, and Islamabad Capital Territory. It aims to support students pursuing Intermediate, Graduation, and Master's level degrees. PEEF was established to address the gap in educational opportunities for deserving students by providing scholarships and other financial assistance.

sources.headings: 4. Punjab Honhaar Scholarship Program
sources.doc: The Honhaar Scholarship Program, an initiative of the Punjab Higher Education Commission, aims to provide financial assistance to deserving and meritorious students pursuing higher education at universities and colleges in Punjab, Pakistan. The program seeks to ensure equal access to quality education, particularly for those with limited financial resources.

sources.headings: 5. HEC Scholarships for MS and PhD students
sources.doc: The Higher Education Commission (HEC) provides liberal scholarships to students desirous of studying for MS and PhD degrees at this university. The scholarship covers tuition fee, monthly stipend, and book allowance.

sources.headings: 2. ICT Scholarships and Balochistan Endowment Scholarships
sources.doc: ICT Scholarships refer to the Prime Minister's National ICT Scholarship Program, a program by Ignite (formerly National ICT R&D Fund) that provides financial assistance to students pursuing ICT degrees. Balochistan Endowment Scholarships, specifically the Balochistan Education Endowment Fund (BEEF), aims to support the education of talented students from Balochistan, including those from less privileged backgrounds.

sources.headings: HEC
sources.doc:
Objectives 
Page Content
  * It is a paradigm shift in a policy of the Government of Pakistan to support undergraduate level students who after completing FA/FSc./Intermediate are unable to pursue university education due to limited financial resources. Unlike past financial assistance schemes that were aimed at MS or PhD programs, the Benazir Undergraduate Scholarship Project focuses on the most critical segment, namely the 4-5year undergraduate programs, which contributes the most to income of the individual who completes the bachelors degree
  * The scholarship covers university tuition fee and stipend throughout four-five years of degree duration. It is a significant step to ensure affordable higher education in all major fields of education including agriculture, arts and humanities, business education, engineering, medical, physical sciences, and social sciences.
  * The project aims to support female education therefore 50% of scholarships are reserved for the female students in the overall Project's target.
  * To encourage physically challenged students, 2% of the scholarships are reserved for them.
  * It is a vibrant program which will facilitate creation of the competent workforce thus enhancing employability factors in youth.
  * It foresees to create drive for education among those students who have discontinued studies due to limited financial issues. 
  * ​By targeting most vulnerable segment of young population through this initiative, poorer households would be enabled to come out of poverty, which in a long run expected to have positive impact on individuals, their families and the community.

sources.headings: PUNJAB EDUCATIONAL ENDOWMENT FUND (PEEF) SCHOLARSHIPS 2024-25, **Eligibility Criteria**
sources.doc:
* Students belonging to the relevant special quota category are eligible to apply.
  * Students who scored at least 60% marks in the Matriculation/Intermediate exams of 2024 (annual), conducted under the Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education or Federal Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education.
  * Students from Federal Government or private registered educational institutions located within the Punjab province can apply.
  * Must be enrolled in a full-time (regular) registered educational institution for Intermediate or Graduation in 2024.
  * Parents’ total monthly income should be Rs. 60,000 or less.
  * Children of government employees in Grades 1 to 4 (if the source of income is only salary) are exempted from the Rs. 60,000 income limit.

sources.headings: BS Computer Science, Admission Criteria, Local and International Applicants
sources.doc:
LUMS is dedicated to enrolling highly accomplished students who possess the potential to make valuable contributions to the learning environment at LUMS and effect positive change in their communities. 
Each successful applicant is made an offer for entry into a particular school at LUMS. Applicants for each school are selected on the basis of the programme requirements of that particular school. Applicants should carefully choose the school(s) and preferred major considering their interests, motivations, academic strengths, and future career paths. 
Applicants who meet the minimum eligibility criteria outlined here for the Undergraduate Programme will be evaluated based on the following criteria: 
  1. Academic Background;
  2. Performance in the Admission Test(s);
  3. Online Application Submission;
  4. Online Submission of Supporting Documents and Fee Payment;
  5. Application Review; and
  6. Interview (if called)


_To be considered for admission evaluation, ensure all steps are completed on or before the stipulated deadline._

sources.headings: BS Computer Science, Can a student apply again if denied admission?
sources.doc: Applicants may reapply to LUMS in the next admission cycle, provided they meet the minimum eligibility criteria mentioned on the website applicable to their academic stream. However, the applicant will need to go through the complete admission process again. Please note that meeting the eligibility criteria does not guarantee admission. sources.headings: BS Computer Science, Applicants with Complete Higher-Secondary Degree
sources.doc:
Applicants who have successfully completed their Higher Secondary degree, i-e, **ICS/FSc/A-Level/High School Diploma** or**International Baccalaureate (IB)** , are eligible to apply for admission if they fulfil one of the following academic qualifications:
  * Successful completion of **Matric** with **70% marks or above** and **FSc/ICS** with **70% marks** or above;
  * **O Level results** (in at least [1](https://lums.edu.pk/programmes/bs-computer-science#one-one)8 subjects) with an average grade of at least ‘B’ in all subjects attempted and **A-Level** (in at least three full-credit A-Level subjects) with an [2](https://lums.edu.pk/programmes/bs-computer-science#one-two)average of 2 Bs and 1 C grade across best three subjects. The three best subjects cannot include any Advanced Subsidiary subjects, the A-Level General Paper, or an A-Level grade less than an E. The full-credit A-level subjects for SBASSE are Biology, Chemistry, Computing, Computer Science, Mathematics, Further Mathematics, Information Technology and Physics.
  * **American High School Diploma (HSD)** with **70% or above** /Grade Point Average of **B or above;**
  * **International Baccalaureate Diploma Programme (IBDP)** [3](https://lums.edu.pk/programmes/bs-computer-science#one-three) with at least **28** out **of 45** points;
  * **International Baccalaureate Career-related** Programme;
  * Combination of the above;
  * Any other equivalent qualification (The Admissions Committee will determine minimum acceptable scores).

If shortlisted for admission, applicants will receive a conditional admission offer. To join LUMS in Fall 2026, applicants must meet all the stipulated conditions specified in the conditional admission offer letter by August 2026.
**Note:**
  * Candidates who have registered or taken the exam of a minimum of three full-credit A Level subjects and do not meet the minimum grades requirement (specified above) must improve their grades in order to be eligible for admission. A-level exams are held in November and June.  To be eligible for admission in **Fall 2026** , applicants must improve their A-level grades in the ****November 2025**** exams.
  * Candidates who have registered or taken the exam of a minimum of three full-credit A-level subjects and do not meet the minimum grades requirement (specified above) and are planning to improve their grades by taking the **June 2026** exams are not eligible for the **Fall 2026** session.
  * Candidates who have already completed their Higher secondary degree (FSc/ICS/High School Diploma/IB, etc.) and do not meet the minimum marks/grades requirement must improve their marks or grades by **November 2025** in order to be eligible for the **Fall 2026** session. 
  * In addition to meeting LUMS' specified conditions, applicants are required to fulfil the academic credential verification requirements of the [Inter Boards Coordination Commission (IBCC)](https://ibcc.edu.pk/), the [Higher Education Commission (HEC) of Pakistan](https://www.hec.gov.pk/english/Pages/default.aspx), or any other relevant authority, including Accreditation Councils.

result.answer: At NUST, admission to the Bachelor of Science in Computer Science can be sought using the NUST Entry Test (NET) or the American College Test (ACT) / Scholastic Aptitude Test (SAT). At NUST, the NET application processing fee for Pakistani or dual nationality holders is Rs. 5,000/- or USD 40/- per exam. At NUST, the ACT/SAT application processing fee for Pakistani or dual nationality holders for National seats is Rs. 5,000/- or USD 40/. At NUST, the ACT/SAT application processing fee for Pakistani or dual nationality holders for International seats is Rs. 10,000/- or USD 80/-. At NUST, the NET application processing fee for Foreign Nationals (Non Pakistani) is Rs. 10,000/- or USD 80/- per exam. At NUST, the NET test is for candidates seeking admission in all Engineering or Computing Programmes.

sources.headings: Bachelors of Science in Computer Science (BSCS)
sources.doc:
**Student Outcomes (SOs)**
  * **1****Academic Education:** To prepare graduates as computing professionals.
  * **2****Knowledge for Solving Computing Problems:** An ability to identify, formulate, research literature, and analyze complex engineering problems reaching substantiated conclusions using first principles of mathematics, natural sciences, and engineering sciences.
  * **3****Problem Analysis:** Identify, formulate, research literature, and solve complex computing problems reaching substantiated conclusions using fundamental principles of mathematics, computing sciences, and relevant domain disciplines.
  * **4****Design/ Development of Solutions:** Design and evaluate solutions for complex computing problems, and design and evaluate systems, components, or processes that meet specified needs with appropriate consideration for public health and safety, cultural, societal, and environmental considerations.
  * **5****Modern Tool Usage:** Create, select, adapt, and apply appropriate techniques, resources, and modern computing tools to complex computing activities, with an understanding of the limitations.
  * **6****Individual and Team Work:** Function effectively as an individual and as a member or leader in diverse teams and multi-disciplinary settings.
  * **7****Communication:** Communicate effectively with the computing community and with society at large about complex computing activities by being able to comprehend and write effective reports, design documentation, make effective presentations, and give and understand clear instructions.
  * **8****Computing Professionalism and Society:** Understand and assess societal, health, safety, legal, and cultural issues within local and global contexts, and the consequential responsibilities relevant to professional computing practice.
  * **9****Ethics:** Understand and commit to professional ethics, responsibilities, and norms of professional computing practice.
  * **10****Life-long Learning:** Recognize the need, and have the ability, to engage in independent learning for continual development as a computing professional.

[**Course Curriculum**](https://seecs.nust.edu.pk/programs/)

sources.headings: Bachelors of Science in Computer Science (BSCS)
sources.doc:
The BSCS program offers appreciably diverse coverage of all related subjects in the fields of computing and mathematics with an adequate number of general education elective courses. To give breadth and depth in the area of computer science, the courses offer to develop the required skills and prepare the graduates to pursue a career in research, higher education, and the software and IT industry. The curriculum has a well-blended combination of courses with knowledge and hands-on experience through labs component. Additionally, there are courses offered in the program to build the students’ personality to make them not only a technology expert but also a good human being contributing positively towards the society. Apart from coursework, the students are facilitated with ample internship opportunities in relevant commercial and industrial organisations, which in turn equip them with the set of dynamic skills required to enter the professional world. The curriculum of the BSCS program instills abilities in students to keep them up-to-date and motivated to learn. The graduates of the program with these skills are competitive not only in Pakistan but also around the World.
The following are the objectives of the undergraduate program in Computer Science:
**Program Educational Objectives (PEOs)**
  * **PEO-1:** Demonstrate sound computer science knowledge and skills.
  * **PEO-2:** Execute and manage teamwork, interpersonal skills, and professional growth.
  * **PEO-3:** Conduct professional practice considering ethical, societal, and environmental aspects.

sources.headings: SALIENT FEATURES OF ADMISSION POLICY FOR UG PROGRAMMES
sources.doc:
* * *
  *   * [ ](https://www.facebook.com/sharer.php?u=https://nust.edu.pk/admissions/undergraduates/salient-features/&t=SALIENT%20FEATURES%20OF%20ADMISSION%20POLICY%20FOR%20UG%20PROGRAMMES "Share on Facebook.")
  * [](https://www.linkedin.com/shareArticle?mini=true&title=SALIENT%20FEATURES%20OF%20ADMISSION%20POLICY%20FOR%20UG%20PROGRAMMES&url=https://nust.edu.pk/admissions/undergraduates/salient-features/ "Share on LinkedIn")

* * *
  * NUST offers admission once in an academic year.

  * Admissions are given on merit only. NUST has a non-discriminatory admission policy and is accessible to all, regardless of ethnicity, religion, disability or gender.

  * Admission can be sought either on the basis of **NUST Entry Test (NET)** or **American College Test** **(ACT)** / **Scholastic Aptitude Test (SAT)** for which limited seats are available.

  * Pakistani nationals (including dual nationality holders) can opt to apply on both **NET** and **ACT** / **SAT** based National & International seats. However, students applying on **ACT** / **SAT** basis for International seats have to pay tuition fee and allied charges a per international student fee structure.

  * Computer-based NET is designed in accordance with the internationally practiced system of on-line examinations. It is easy to attempt with minimal practice.

  * NET is compiled from text books prescribed for HSSC courses. Candidates preparing for NET are advised to consult all relevant text books of various boards of education.

  * Instructions to attempt computer-based entry test and sample test are available on NUST website for guidance.

  * The pattern and the standard of question papers for both types of tests is the same.
  * NET is conducted at **four** locations, Islamabad (NUST Campus), Karachi, Quetta and Gilgit.
  * At **Islamabad** and **Quetta,** the test is conducted in computer-based format and in **Karachi** and **Gilgit,** in paper-based format.
  * Detailed schedule can be viewed by visiting [**NET Schedule**](https://nust.edu.pk/admissions/undergraduates/dates-to-remember/).

  * Candidates can appear in entry test more than once to improve their score with the provision that during a series test can only be taken once for a particular discipline. In case of multiple attempts of NET the best test score will be considered for merit generation.

  * For computer-based NET, candidates can choose the date and session of test from the available schedule.

  * The result of NET will remain valid for the current admission cycle only.

  * For Registration:- 
    * FA / FSc stream candidates should have passed HSSC Part-I exam. For those candidates who have completed their HSSC should have minimum 60% marks. All candidates must have 60% marks in SSC as well.
    * A level students who are in second year of study should have minimum 60% marks as per equivalence of O level certificate issued by IBCC.

  * For detailed eligibility criteria please visit [Undergraduate Admissions section](https://nust.edu.pk/admissions/undergraduates/eligibility-criteria-for-ug-programmes/).

  * Application Processing Fee will be charged as follows:- 
    * For NUST Entry Test (per exam) – Rs. 5,000/- or USD 40/-
    * For ACT / SAT based National seat – Rs. 5,000/- or USD 40/-
    * For ACT / SAT based International seat – Rs. 10,000/- or USD 80/-
    * For Foreign Nationals NET (per exam) – Rs. 10,000/- or USD 80/-

| Mathematics  | **​50%**  |

  * The test is for candidates seeking admission in all **Engineering** or **Computing Programmes**.
  * Such candidates can also opt for admission in **BS Bioinformatics, BS Mathematics, BS Physics, BS Chemistry and BS Food Science & Technology** programmes without payment of additional registration fee and appearing in a separate NET.
  * Candidates having **Pre-Engineering with Additional Bio** OR **Pre-Medical with Additional Math** OR equivalent, applying for **Engineering** or **Computing Programmes** will appear in **NET-Engineering** paper.
  * * Candidates of **Pre-Medical group** / equivalent qualification applying for **Engineering programmes** without taking additional math exam will appear in **NET-Engineering paper**. However, it is **mandatory** to clear the condensed Mathematics course of 8 x weeks offered by NUST, prior to admission. To register for the course, please visit <https://connected.nust.edu.pk/enrol/index.php?id=186>.
  * * Candidates of **Pre-Medical group** / equivalent qualification applying for **Computing Programmes** without taking additional math exam will appear in **NET – Engineering** paper.
  * Candidates having HSSC / equivalent with **Mathematics** as one of the major subject applying for **Computing Programmes** will also appear in **NET-Engineering** paper.

sources.headings: Fee Structure for International Students (In USD):
sources.doc:
|  ​ ​All UG Programmes  |  
| --- |  
| ​Admission Processing Fee (Non-Refundable)  | ​USD 600  |  
| ​Tuition Fee (per annum)  | ​USD 5,400  |  
| ​Security Deposit (Refundable)  | ​USD 250  |  
| ​Health facilities (per annum)  | ​USD 120  |  
  * Tuition fee for the first academic year (two semesters) will be deposited as per selection letter.
  * Subsequent, tuition fee will be paid through challan form generated by Finance Directorate, NUST.
  * The security deposit is payable along with the admission processing fee at the time of admission.
  * Course repeat/Improvement/summer semester Fee is USD 40 per credit hour.
  * “**SWIFT Message** ” from sender Bank is essentially required in case money is transferred from abroad.
  * “Harvard Business school licensing fee” will be charged to undergraduate students of BBA, BS Accounting & Finance and BS Tourism & Hospitality Management @ USD 50 Per year.


**Note** : All fees and other charges are subject to revision from time to time.

sources.headings: Frequently Asked Questions - FAST NUCES Admissions Fall 2026
sources.doc:
**Q:** How Can I Apply for Admission?
**A:** The procedure for admission is as follows: 
  * Apply online only through the official portal.
  * No applications via post or hand are accepted.
  * Each applicant receives a unique ARN (Application Reference Number).
  * Ensure all information is correct before submission.
  * **Verify all information carefully before making fee payment.**
  * Any changes after fee submission may incur processing charges.
  * Incorrect or false information may lead to cancellation without refund.
  * Admit card is generated after fee payment.
  * Candidate must appear at the scheduled test center.

**Important:** Admission of a student automatically stands cancelled if he or she fails in the required exam whose result was not available at the time of admission application. 
[🔗 https://nu.edu.pk/Degree-Programs](https://nu.edu.pk/Degree-Programs) [🔗 https://nu.edu.pk/Admissions/Schedule](https://nu.edu.pk/Admissions/Schedule)
**Q:** Which admission tests are accepted for Fall 2026?
**A:** Applicants may apply through: 
  * SAT/NTS **OR** NU Admission Test (Undergraduate Admissions)   
_(Applicant must select**only one** out of the three admission test options)_
  * HAT-1, 2 & 3 (Graduate Admissions) **OR** NU Admission Test   
_(Applicant must select**only one** out of the two admission test options)_
  * HAT-Subject for PhD **OR** NU Admission Test   
_(Applicant must select**only one** out of the two admission test options)_

**Q:** What is the fee per credit hour?
**A:** **Rs 12,000 per credit hour** (w.e.f Fall 2026, applicable to all batches) 
**Q:** How is semester fee calculated?
**A:** FAST does not have a fixed semester fee.  
Example: 
  * 15 credit hours × Rs. 12,000
  * Student Activity Fund

**Q:** Are there any additional fees?
**A:** At admission: 
  * Admission fee
  * Security deposit
  * First semester tuition fee
  * Student Activity Fund

Later semesters: 
  * Tuition fee
  * Student Activity Fund

**Q:** I cannot afford the fee. Is financial assistance available?
**A:** Yes: 
  * Need-based financial aid
  * Interest-free loans
  * Merit scholarships

**Q:** Can fees be paid in installments?
**A:** Yes, subject to approval by campus administration. 
**Q:** What is the refund policy?
**A:**
  * Admission fee is non-refundable
  * Security deposit is refundable at the time of completion of degree or closing of admission
  * Tuition Fee is refunded in accordance with the guidelines of HEC

[🔗 https://nu.edu.pk/Admissions/FeeStructure](https://nu.edu.pk/Admissions/FeeStructure)
**Q:** Which campuses have hostel facilities?
**A:** Hostels are available at: 
  * Chiniot-Faisalabad
  * Multan
  * Peshawar

**Q:** Is transport facility available?
**A:** Yes, transport facility is available in all campuses.

**A:** Monday to Friday (8:00 AM to 4:00 PM) 
**Q:** I am unable to upload documents. What should I do?
**A:**
  * Ensure JPG/JPEG format
  * File size must be under 1MB
  * Contact admissions@nu.edu.pk

**Q:** I uploaded the wrong document. How can I correct it?
**A:** Email the relevant campus admissions office. Post-submission changes may involve processing charges. 
**Q:** How can I pay the admission fee?
**A:**
  * Bank deposit
  * KuickPay online system

**A:**

**Q:** When will test results be announced?
**A:**
  * Results can be checked on the admission portal
  * SMS/email notifications may also be sent

**Q:** I am a foreign student. How can I apply?
**A:**
  * Passport number can be used
  * Afghan students may use POR number

**Q:** Can I transfer from another university?
**A:** Yes: 
  * Apply as a normal applicant
  * Credit transfer after admission
  * Maximum 50% credits transferable (HEC rule)

**Q:** Can I migrate between campuses?
**A:** Yes, subject to: 
  * Merit
  * Seat availability
  * Approval

**Q:** Are classes held on weekends or evenings?
**A:**
  * Karachi offers weekend programs
  * Other campuses may offer limited evening/weekend classes

**Q:** How is merit calculated?
**A:**
  * Based on Admission Test / SAT / NTS / HAT **OR** NU Admission Test   
_(Applicant must select**only one** out of the three admission test options)_
  * Academic record (SSC + HSSC / Bachelor)

[🔗 https://nu.edu.pk/Admissions/EligibilityCriteria](https://nu.edu.pk/Admissions/EligibilityCriteria)

result.answer: At LUMS, for Fall 2026 admissions, SAT scores taken before March 2024 will not be considered, and ACT scores taken before February 2024 will not be considered. Official ACT scores must be submitted directly using college code 7896. For financial aid, LUMS accepts a Financial Aid Application as part of the admissions process if applicable, but the sources do not specify what types or amounts of financial aid are available.

sources.headings: BS Economics and Mathematics (Joint Major), Important Note
sources.doc:
1. LUMS will only accept scores of the Admission Test(s) mentioned above for the Fall 2026 applications.
  2. **SAT/ACT** taken after the stipulated deadlines will not be considered for the Fall 2026 admissions.
  3. **SAT** taken before **March 2024** will not be considered for Fall 2026 admissions.
  4. **ACT** taken before **February 2024** will not be considered for Fall 2026 admissions.
  5. While registering for the SAT/ACT/LCAT, use your name as it appears on your LUMS Online application and other academic credentials. Using a different name may prevent your scores from matching the rest of your application in our database.
  6. **Official SAT scores** of all applicants must be submitted by the testing agency, i.e.,**ETS** , directly to the LUMS Admissions Office. Applicants must request ETS to send a direct report to LUMS. The college code for reporting SAT scores to LUMS is **0513**.
  7. **Official ACT scores** must be submitted directly to the LUMS Admissions Office by the testing agency, i.e., American College Testing Service (ACT), USA. The college code for reporting ACT scores to LUMS is **7896**.
  8. Applicants are required to report test scores of all attempts through an online application and must submit a copy of the score report(s) to the University. Scores and attempts not reported through the LUMS Online application will not be considered valid for evaluation.
  9. **The best score of a single attempt** (SAT and/or ACT) will be considered for application evaluation.
  10. Applicants are required to submit score(s) of the SAT and/or ACT to the LUMS Admissions Office soon after the announcement of the results. A copy of a “**Student Report** ” should also be uploaded online.
  11. LCAT Scores will be valid only for **One (1) academic year**.
  12. LCAT scores will be used for application evaluation and, hence, will not be disclosed to applicants.
  13. Applicants taking the LUMS Admission Test(s), and those who have also taken (or are planning to take) the SAT and/or ACT tests are encouraged to submit a copy of their standardized test score report(s) as part of their admission application. A copy of the scores should be uploaded online along with all other supporting documents, or reported directly from the Testing Agency.

sources.headings: BS Economics and Mathematics (Joint Major), Test Requirements, LCAT Guidelines
sources.doc:
The LCAT is a paper-based, multiple-choice test, similar to the SAT, though it may differ in terms of duration and format.
  * **Number of Sections:** 4 (two verbal and two math sections)
  * **Duration:** The duration of each section is 40 minutes, with a total test duration of approximately 3 hours.
  * **Test Mode:** LCAT is a paper-based test.
  * **Calculators:** Not allowed during any part of the test.


**Verbal Sections**
The Verbal Sections of the LCAT evaluate critical reading and writing skills essential for academic and professional success. These sections test comprehension, analysis, and effective communication through various content domains, including Craft and Structure, Information and Ideas, Standard English Conventions, and Expression of Ideas. Applicants are encouraged to practice reading comprehension, text analysis, and editing for clarity and accuracy.
**Math Sections**
The Math Sections of the LCAT evaluate essential mathematical skills required for higher education, focusing on Algebra, Advanced Mathematics, Problem-Solving and Data Analysis, and Geometry and Trigonometry, which are critical for success in higher education. These sections test quantitative reasoning, data interpretation, and problem-solving abilities. Applicants are advised to strengthen foundational concepts, practice problem-solving without calculators, and review SAT-style materials for effective preparation.
[Click here](https://lums.edu.pk/sites/default/files/sample_lcat_2025.pdf) to access the LCAT guidelines and explore sample questions for both the Math and Verbal sections.

sources.headings: FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS (FAQS)
sources.doc:
* * *
  *   * [ ](https://www.facebook.com/sharer.php?u=https://nust.edu.pk/admissions/scholarships/frequently-asked-questions-faqs/&t=FREQUENTLY%20ASKED%20QUESTIONS%20\(FAQS\) "Share on Facebook.")
  * [](https://www.linkedin.com/shareArticle?mini=true&title=FREQUENTLY%20ASKED%20QUESTIONS%20\(FAQS\)&url=https://nust.edu.pk/admissions/scholarships/frequently-asked-questions-faqs/ "Share on LinkedIn")

* * *
**Q. How many types of financial aid are offered?​​**
  * There are three types of financial aid offered by NUST: 
    * Need based scholarships.
    * Merit based scholarships / financial assistance.
    * Interest free loans.

**Q. When and How to Apply for Financial Aid?​​**
  * Under Graduate (UG) & Masters (MS) candidates apply for financial aid immediately after submitting online admission application.
  * To apply candidates are required to submit online NUST need Based Financial Aid Application Form (NFAAF).
  * Due date for submitting NFAAF is the same as that of the online admission application. Due date for MS & UG is tentatively May & June 2022 respectively. Please visit NUST admission portal for exact dates.
  * Financial Aid Applications will not be accepted separately after due date.

**Q. Who can apply for financial aid?​​**
  * All UG & Masters candidate(s) are eligible to apply for financial aid​ at the time of admission.

**Q. Does applying for financial aid have any effect on admission application?**
**OR**
**I have completed my admission application but I have not filled / partially filled the financial aid application and I am not interested to apply for financial aid. Will leaving the financial aid form unfilled / partially filled, effect my admission application?​​**
  * No, financial aid application has no effect on admission decision.

**Q. What is meant by physical verification?** ​​
  * NUST team may visit your house, business premises or carry out inquiry from the surrounding neighbors to ​physically verify facts stated by you while applying for financial aid. Physical Verification may be carried out at any point of time during academic life cycle at NUST.

**Q. I have submitted NFAAF and attached soft copies of supporting documents too, do I need to send hard copies of supporting documents? If yes, When?** ​​
  * You do not need to send supporting documents to FAO immediately after submitting NFAAF.
  * After due processing, FAO will inform you via email to mail the documents in hard form, within a due date. Failure to provide documents within due date will lead to cancellation of NFAAF.

**Q. I want to apply for​ other need based scholarships like PEEF, CMEEF KPK, FEF etc. Do I need to submit another application form?​​**
  * Upon submitting NFAAF, you will be considered for all types of need based scholarships. FAO will inform you incase any additional form / document is required.

**Q. I do not have few of the supporting documents. What should i do?**
**OR**
**I need more time to arrange the supporting documents. Please allow me to submit NFAAF and provide supporting documents in a few more working days.​​​**
  * You may attach scan copy of a hand written letter of explanation​ (duly signed by you and your parent / guardian).
  * Briefly explain reason of not attaching the supporting document and expected date till you will provide the same to Financial Aid Office.

sources.doc:
1. LUMS will only accept scores of the Admission Test(s) mentioned above for the Fall 2026 applications.
  2. **SAT/ACT** taken after the stipulated deadlines will not be considered for the Fall 2026 admissions.
  3. **SAT** taken before **March 2024** will not be considered for Fall 2026 admissions.
  4. **ACT** taken before **February 2024** will not be considered for Fall 2026 admissions.
  5. While registering for the SAT/ACT/LCAT, use your name as it appears on your LUMS Online application and other academic credentials. Using a different name may prevent your scores from matching the rest of your application in our database.
  6. **Official SAT scores** of all applicants must be submitted by the testing agency, i.e.,**ETS** , directly to the LUMS Admissions Office. Applicants must request ETS to send a direct report to LUMS. The college code for reporting SAT scores to LUMS is **0513**.
  7. **Official ACT scores** must be submitted directly to the LUMS Admissions Office by the testing agency, i.e., American College Testing Service (ACT), USA. The college code for reporting ACT scores to LUMS is **7896**.
  8. Applicants are required to report test scores of all attempts through an online application and must submit a copy of the score report(s) to the University. Scores and attempts not reported through the LUMS Online application will not be considered valid for evaluation.
  9. **The best score of a single attempt** (SAT and/or ACT) will be considered for application evaluation.
  10. Applicants are required to submit score(s) of the SAT and/or ACT to the LUMS Admissions Office soon after the announcement of the results. A copy of a “**Student Report** ” should also be uploaded online.
  11. LCAT Scores will be valid only for **One (1) academic year**.
  12. LCAT scores will be used for application evaluation and, hence, will not be disclosed to applicants.
  13. Applicants taking the LUMS Admission Test(s), and those who have also taken (or are planning to take) the SAT and/or ACT tests are encouraged to submit a copy of their standardized test score report(s) as part of their admission application. A copy of the scores should be uploaded online along with all other supporting documents, or reported directly from the Testing Agency.

item.query: What is the FAST entry test pattern and what percentage do I need in FSc to apply for BS AI?
item.gt: English 10%, Analytical 20%, Basic Math 20%, Advanced Math 50%, with negative marking; HSSC 50% minimum (SSC 60%) with Mathematics

result.answer:
The FAST-NU admission test has sections with varying weightage. For BS (CS/Engg.) including BS AI, the pattern is: English 10%, Analytical Skills & IQ 20%, Basic Math 20%, and Advanced Math 50% (Source 10). 

For BS Artificial Intelligence, applicants must have 50% minimum marks in HSSC (FSc) or equivalent examination (Source 12). 

Applicants can take either the FAST-NUCES test or SAT test for computing programs (Source 12). NTS NAT-IE and NAT-ICS tests from specific universities will not be acceptable (Source 12).

claims.text: For BS (CS/Engg.) programs, English accounts for 10% of the admission test
For BS (CS/Engg.) programs, Analytical Skills & IQ accounts for 20% of the admission test
For BS (CS/Engg.) programs, Basic Math accounts for 20% of the admission test
For BS (CS/Engg.) programs, Advanced Math accounts for 50% of the admission test
For BS Artificial Intelligence, applicants must achieve 50% minimum marks in HSSC or equivalent examination
Applicants to BS Computing programs must select only one of three admission test options: FAST-NUCES, SAT, or NTS NAT-IE/NAT-ICS
NTS tests from specific universities will not be acceptable for BS (CS/Engg.) programs

item.query: Compare the first-year cost of BS Computer Science at LUMS and NUST.
item.gt: LUMS first year total PKR 2,182,200 (tuition 1,557,200); NUST tuition 216,750 per semester plus 35,000 admission processing and 10,000 security; bases differ (annual vs per-semester) and must be stated

result.answer: At LUMS, the total fees listed in the FY 2026-27 Fee Structure table for BS Computer Science amount to 2,182,200 PKR. At LUMS, the per credit hour rate for FY 2026–27 is PKR 45,800. At NUST, international students pay 5,400 USD tuition per annum.

sources.headings: BS Computer Science, Major Preference
sources.doc:
Applicants may apply for admission to any **two Schools** through a single application. 
Applicants are required to indicate their Major preference(s) for the BS Programmes at the Syed Babar Ali School of Science and Engineering (SBASSE), and their Department and Major preferences for the BA/BSc (Honours) Programmes at the Mushtaq Ahmad Gurmani School of Humanities and Social Sciences (MGSHSS) and the Suleman Dawood School of Business (SDSB) through the LUMS Online Admission Application Form. 
**Students are admitted to a specific School** based on **merit** and the **availability of seats**. At the time of admission, students are not assigned a Major, except for those admitted to the following: 
  * BA-LL.B. Programme in the Shaikh Ahmad Hassan School of Law (SAHSOL); and 
  * Certain students may be offered admission to a specialist stream in the Syed Babar Ali School of Science and Engineering (SBASSE). These students will be permitted to change their field of study only to a limited set of approved Majors, should they choose to do so, at the end of their First Year. 


Students may request a change in their Programme or School at the end of their First Year at LUMS, subject to their academic performance and the availability of seats. Such requests will be considered on a case-by-case basis and reviewed by the relevant Department or School in accordance with the University’s approved policy.
The allocation of a preferred Major shall not be guaranteed at the time of admission. The final allocation of a Major shall be undertaken in accordance with the School’s approved policy and procedures, and shall be determined primarily on the basis of the student’s stated preferences, academic performance during the first year of study at LUMS, and, where applicable, the availability of seats in the selected Major. 
For the **BA/BSc (Honours) Programmes offered by the Mushtaq Ahmad Gurmani School of Humanities and Social Sciences (MGSHSS)** , students shall be admitted into **one of two designated admission streams:** **Humanities and Social Sciences (HSS)** or **Economics (ECON),** based on the preferences indicated in their online application. Transfers between the two are not possible, except in exceptional circumstances and in the event that seats are available, which in the Economics stream is rare.

sources.headings: BS Computer Science, Is it possible to transfer credits from another university to LUMS?
sources.doc:
Yes, LUMS accepts transfer students from accredited institutions at the undergraduate level. Applicants interested in transfer to the LUMS undergraduate programmes should be enrolled in an undergraduate programme in an HEC recognised institution and should have completed one year or expected to complete one year before joining as a full time student. Transfer is offered twice a year before the Fall and Spring semesters respectively.
Please visit the mentioned link <https://admission.lums.edu.pk/programmes/transfer> for detailed information.

No, attending the first semester at LUMS is compulsory and deferment is not an option for undergraduates.

**Student Outcomes (SOs)**
  * **1****Academic Education:** To prepare graduates as computing professionals.
  * **2****Knowledge for Solving Computing Problems:** An ability to identify, formulate, research literature, and analyze complex engineering problems reaching substantiated conclusions using first principles of mathematics, natural sciences, and engineering sciences.
  * **3****Problem Analysis:** Identify, formulate, research literature, and solve complex computing problems reaching substantiated conclusions using fundamental principles of mathematics, computing sciences, and relevant domain disciplines.
  * **4****Design/ Development of Solutions:** Design and evaluate solutions for complex computing problems, and design and evaluate systems, components, or processes that meet specified needs with appropriate consideration for public health and safety, cultural, societal, and environmental considerations.
  * **5****Modern Tool Usage:** Create, select, adapt, and apply appropriate techniques, resources, and modern computing tools to complex computing activities, with an understanding of the limitations.
  * **6****Individual and Team Work:** Function effectively as an individual and as a member or leader in diverse teams and multi-disciplinary settings.
  * **7****Communication:** Communicate effectively with the computing community and with society at large about complex computing activities by being able to comprehend and write effective reports, design documentation, make effective presentations, and give and understand clear instructions.
  * **8****Computing Professionalism and Society:** Understand and assess societal, health, safety, legal, and cultural issues within local and global contexts, and the consequential responsibilities relevant to professional computing practice.
  * **9****Ethics:** Understand and commit to professional ethics, responsibilities, and norms of professional computing practice.
  * **10****Life-long Learning:** Recognize the need, and have the ability, to engage in independent learning for continual development as a computing professional.

sources.headings: Bachelors of Science in Computer Science (BSCS)
sources.doc:
The BSCS program offers appreciably diverse coverage of all related subjects in the fields of computing and mathematics with an adequate number of general education elective courses. To give breadth and depth in the area of computer science, the courses offer to develop the required skills and prepare the graduates to pursue a career in research, higher education, and the software and IT industry. The curriculum has a well-blended combination of courses with knowledge and hands-on experience through labs component. Additionally, there are courses offered in the program to build the students’ personality to make them not only a technology expert but also a good human being contributing positively towards the society. Apart from coursework, the students are facilitated with ample internship opportunities in relevant commercial and industrial organisations, which in turn equip them with the set of dynamic skills required to enter the professional world. The curriculum of the BSCS program instills abilities in students to keep them up-to-date and motivated to learn. The graduates of the program with these skills are competitive not only in Pakistan but also around the World.
The following are the objectives of the undergraduate program in Computer Science:
**Program Educational Objectives (PEOs)**
  * **PEO-1:** Demonstrate sound computer science knowledge and skills.
  * **PEO-2:** Execute and manage teamwork, interpersonal skills, and professional growth.
  * **PEO-3:** Conduct professional practice considering ethical, societal, and environmental aspects.

sources.headings: SALIENT FEATURES OF ADMISSION POLICY FOR UG PROGRAMMES
sources.doc:
* * *
  *   * [ ](https://www.facebook.com/sharer.php?u=https://nust.edu.pk/admissions/undergraduates/salient-features/&t=SALIENT%20FEATURES%20OF%20ADMISSION%20POLICY%20FOR%20UG%20PROGRAMMES "Share on Facebook.")
  * [](https://www.linkedin.com/shareArticle?mini=true&title=SALIENT%20FEATURES%20OF%20ADMISSION%20POLICY%20FOR%20UG%20PROGRAMMES&url=https://nust.edu.pk/admissions/undergraduates/salient-features/ "Share on LinkedIn")

* * *
  * NUST offers admission once in an academic year.

  * Admissions are given on merit only. NUST has a non-discriminatory admission policy and is accessible to all, regardless of ethnicity, religion, disability or gender.

  * Admission can be sought either on the basis of **NUST Entry Test (NET)** or **American College Test** **(ACT)** / **Scholastic Aptitude Test (SAT)** for which limited seats are available.

  * Pakistani nationals (including dual nationality holders) can opt to apply on both **NET** and **ACT** / **SAT** based National & International seats. However, students applying on **ACT** / **SAT** basis for International seats have to pay tuition fee and allied charges a per international student fee structure.

  * Computer-based NET is designed in accordance with the internationally practiced system of on-line examinations. It is easy to attempt with minimal practice.

  * NET is compiled from text books prescribed for HSSC courses. Candidates preparing for NET are advised to consult all relevant text books of various boards of education.

  * Instructions to attempt computer-based entry test and sample test are available on NUST website for guidance.

  * The pattern and the standard of question papers for both types of tests is the same.
  * NET is conducted at **four** locations, Islamabad (NUST Campus), Karachi, Quetta and Gilgit.
  * At **Islamabad** and **Quetta,** the test is conducted in computer-based format and in **Karachi** and **Gilgit,** in paper-based format.
  * Detailed schedule can be viewed by visiting [**NET Schedule**](https://nust.edu.pk/admissions/undergraduates/dates-to-remember/).

  * Candidates can appear in entry test more than once to improve their score with the provision that during a series test can only be taken once for a particular discipline. In case of multiple attempts of NET the best test score will be considered for merit generation.

  * For computer-based NET, candidates can choose the date and session of test from the available schedule.

  * The result of NET will remain valid for the current admission cycle only.

  * For Registration:- 
    * FA / FSc stream candidates should have passed HSSC Part-I exam. For those candidates who have completed their HSSC should have minimum 60% marks. All candidates must have 60% marks in SSC as well.
    * A level students who are in second year of study should have minimum 60% marks as per equivalence of O level certificate issued by IBCC.

  * For detailed eligibility criteria please visit [Undergraduate Admissions section](https://nust.edu.pk/admissions/undergraduates/eligibility-criteria-for-ug-programmes/).

  * Application Processing Fee will be charged as follows:- 
    * For NUST Entry Test (per exam) – Rs. 5,000/- or USD 40/-
    * For ACT / SAT based National seat – Rs. 5,000/- or USD 40/-
    * For ACT / SAT based International seat – Rs. 10,000/- or USD 80/-
    * For Foreign Nationals NET (per exam) – Rs. 10,000/- or USD 80/-

item.query: LUMS aur FAST mein CS ke liye minimum marks ka kya farq hai?
item.gt: LUMS: Matric 70% and FSc/ICS 70%; FAST: SSC 60% and HSSC 50% with Mathematics

result.answer: Apne current resources se, main sirf LUMS University ki requirements provide kar sakta hoon. FAST University ke admission criteria ke liye ye sources mein koi information nahi hai, isliye comparison nahi kar sakta. LUMS ke BS Computer Science ke liye, applicants akamaiatoriamente: (1) Matric aur FSc/ICS dono mein 70% marks (Source 1, Source 3), (2) IB mein 28/45 points (Source 1, Source 3), (3) O-Level average grade 'B' (Source 1, Source 3), (4) American High School Diploma 70% ya B Grade (Source 1, Source 3). Ye structured rahen: LUMS BS CS ke liye minimum 70% FSc ke sath Matric chahiye, aur FSc ke 70% ke upar hona zaroori hai (Source 1, 3). Ye claims sahi hain sirf in sources se: LUMS has minimum 70% requirement for Matric and FSc/ICS (Source 1, 3). LUMS has 28/45 points for IB (Source 1, 3). FAST requirements nahi available in provided sources.

claims.text: LUMS BS Computer Science ke liye applicants ko Matric aur FSc/ICS dono mein kam se kam 70% marks chahiye hain.

sources.headings: BS Computer Science, Applicants with Complete Higher-Secondary Degree
sources.doc:
Applicants who have successfully completed their Higher Secondary degree, i-e, **ICS/FSc/A-Level/High School Diploma** or**International Baccalaureate (IB)** , are eligible to apply for admission if they fulfil one of the following academic qualifications:
  * Successful completion of **Matric** with **70% marks or above** and **FSc/ICS** with **70% marks** or above;
  * **O Level results** (in at least [1](https://lums.edu.pk/programmes/bs-computer-science#one-one)8 subjects) with an average grade of at least ‘B’ in all subjects attempted and **A-Level** (in at least three full-credit A-Level subjects) with an [2](https://lums.edu.pk/programmes/bs-computer-science#one-two)average of 2 Bs and 1 C grade across best three subjects. The three best subjects cannot include any Advanced Subsidiary subjects, the A-Level General Paper, or an A-Level grade less than an E. The full-credit A-level subjects for SBASSE are Biology, Chemistry, Computing, Computer Science, Mathematics, Further Mathematics, Information Technology and Physics.
  * **American High School Diploma (HSD)** with **70% or above** /Grade Point Average of **B or above;**
  * **International Baccalaureate Diploma Programme (IBDP)** [3](https://lums.edu.pk/programmes/bs-computer-science#one-three) with at least **28** out **of 45** points;
  * **International Baccalaureate Career-related** Programme;
  * Combination of the above;
  * Any other equivalent qualification (The Admissions Committee will determine minimum acceptable scores).

If shortlisted for admission, applicants will receive a conditional admission offer. To join LUMS in Fall 2026, applicants must meet all the stipulated conditions specified in the conditional admission offer letter by August 2026.
**Note:**
  * Candidates who have registered or taken the exam of a minimum of three full-credit A Level subjects and do not meet the minimum grades requirement (specified above) must improve their grades in order to be eligible for admission. A-level exams are held in November and June.  To be eligible for admission in **Fall 2026** , applicants must improve their A-level grades in the ****November 2025**** exams.
  * Candidates who have registered or taken the exam of a minimum of three full-credit A-level subjects and do not meet the minimum grades requirement (specified above) and are planning to improve their grades by taking the **June 2026** exams are not eligible for the **Fall 2026** session.
  * Candidates who have already completed their Higher secondary degree (FSc/ICS/High School Diploma/IB, etc.) and do not meet the minimum marks/grades requirement must improve their marks or grades by **November 2025** in order to be eligible for the **Fall 2026** session. 
  * In addition to meeting LUMS' specified conditions, applicants are required to fulfil the academic credential verification requirements of the [Inter Boards Coordination Commission (IBCC)](https://ibcc.edu.pk/), the [Higher Education Commission (HEC) of Pakistan](https://www.hec.gov.pk/english/Pages/default.aspx), or any other relevant authority, including Accreditation Councils.

BS Computer Science, Major Preference
sources.doc:
Applicants may apply for admission to any **two Schools** through a single application. 
Applicants are required to indicate their Major preference(s) for the BS Programmes at the Syed Babar Ali School of Science and Engineering (SBASSE), and their Department and Major preferences for the BA/BSc (Honours) Programmes at the Mushtaq Ahmad Gurmani School of Humanities and Social Sciences (MGSHSS) and the Suleman Dawood School of Business (SDSB) through the LUMS Online Admission Application Form. 
**Students are admitted to a specific School** based on **merit** and the **availability of seats**. At the time of admission, students are not assigned a Major, except for those admitted to the following: 
  * BA-LL.B. Programme in the Shaikh Ahmad Hassan School of Law (SAHSOL); and 
  * Certain students may be offered admission to a specialist stream in the Syed Babar Ali School of Science and Engineering (SBASSE). These students will be permitted to change their field of study only to a limited set of approved Majors, should they choose to do so, at the end of their First Year. 


Students may request a change in their Programme or School at the end of their First Year at LUMS, subject to their academic performance and the availability of seats. Such requests will be considered on a case-by-case basis and reviewed by the relevant Department or School in accordance with the University’s approved policy.
The allocation of a preferred Major shall not be guaranteed at the time of admission. The final allocation of a Major shall be undertaken in accordance with the School’s approved policy and procedures, and shall be determined primarily on the basis of the student’s stated preferences, academic performance during the first year of study at LUMS, and, where applicable, the availability of seats in the selected Major. 
For the **BA/BSc (Honours) Programmes offered by the Mushtaq Ahmad Gurmani School of Humanities and Social Sciences (MGSHSS)** , students shall be admitted into **one of two designated admission streams:** **Humanities and Social Sciences (HSS)** or **Economics (ECON),** based on the preferences indicated in their online application. Transfers between the two are not possible, except in exceptional circumstances and in the event that seats are available, which in the Economics stream is rare.
